common_name: Jack Snipe Daffodil (Reflexed White-and-Yellow Cyclamineus Daffodil)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall; Jack Snipe is an early, dwarf Cyclamineus-type daffodil with strongly swept-back petals.

directions: Plant bulbs 6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Jack Snipe bears white petals swept sharply backward from a bright yellow trumpet, the characteristic wind-blown look of Narcissus cyclamineus hybrids, opening early in the season on short, sturdy stems well suited to rock gardens, containers, and the front of a border. Its compact size and early bloom make it a good companion to later, taller daffodils for an extended spring display. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally without braiding or cutting it, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply over the years.

common_name: Baby Moon Daffodil (Miniature Fragrant Late Yellow Jonquil)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall; Baby Moon is a miniature, late-blooming, fragrant jonquilla daffodil well suited to naturalizing in warm climates.

directions: Plant bulbs 4-6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Baby Moon bears small, clear yellow, sweetly fragrant flowers on very short stems, blooming later than most daffodils in a miniature jonquilla form that fits neatly into rock gardens, containers, and the front of a border. As a jonquilla-type it tends to naturalize and perennialize especially well in mild-winter climates like the Gulf South, where many large trumpet daffodils fail to return reliably. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally without braiding or cutting it, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply over the years.

common_name: Actaea Daffodil (Fragrant White Poet's Daffodil with Red-Rimmed Eye)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall; Actaea is a poeticus-type daffodil, among the latest and most fragrant daffodils to bloom, with a small red-rimmed yellow eye.

directions: Plant bulbs 6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Actaea bears flat, pure white petals surrounding a small, flat, yellow cup edged in a fine red rim, the classic Poet's Narcissus form, opening late in the daffodil season with an intense, sweet fragrance considered among the finest of any daffodil. Poeticus types like Actaea have a long garden history and naturalize well in meadows and orchards. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally without braiding or cutting it, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply over the years.

common_name: Geranium Daffodil (Fragrant White Tazetta with Orange-Red Cup)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall; Geranium is a classic tazetta daffodil bearing multiple intensely fragrant flowers per stem, well suited to the mild winters of the Gulf South.

directions: Plant bulbs 6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Geranium bears clusters of three to five white flowers per stem, each centered with a small, ruffled orange-red cup, carrying a powerful, sweet fragrance typical of tazetta daffodils and blooming reliably even in the mild winters of the Gulf South, where many large trumpet daffodils fail to naturalize. Its multi-flowered habit makes each stem a small bouquet in itself, excellent for cutting. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally without braiding or cutting it, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply over the years.

common_name: Minnow Daffodil (Miniature Multi-Flowered Pale Yellow Tazetta)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall; Minnow is a true miniature tazetta daffodil with several pale flowers per stem, well suited to containers and rock gardens.

directions: Plant bulbs 4-6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Minnow bears clusters of small, pale cream-yellow flowers with slightly deeper yellow cups on very short stems, a true miniature tazetta daffodil that fits neatly into containers, troughs, and the front of a border where full-size daffodils would be out of scale. Like other tazetta types it perennializes well in mild-winter climates. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally without braiding or cutting it, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply over the years.

common_name: Rip Van Winkle Daffodil (Shaggy Double Miniature Heirloom Daffodil)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall; Rip van Winkle is a shaggy, fully double heirloom miniature daffodil dating to the 19th century.

directions: Plant bulbs 4-6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Rip van Winkle bears small, shaggy, fully double golden-yellow flowers with narrow, twisted petals that give the bloom an unruly, tousled appearance quite unlike the neat, formal shape of most daffodils, a distinctive 19th-century heirloom that has remained in cultivation for its charm and novelty. Its miniature size suits rock gardens and containers. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally without braiding or cutting it, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply over the years.

common_name: Beersheba Daffodil (Historic 1923 Pure White Trumpet Daffodil)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall; introduced in 1923 by Guy Wilson, Beersheba was one of the first truly pure white trumpet daffodils.

directions: Plant bulbs 6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Introduced in 1923 by the renowned Irish breeder Guy Wilson, Beersheba was one of the first daffodils to achieve a truly pure, unbroken white trumpet and perianth, a milestone in daffodil breeding history that opened the door to the many all-white trumpet cultivars grown today. Its elegant, classic form and historic significance have kept it in specialty bulb catalogs for a century. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally without braiding or cutting it, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply over the years.
